transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with the table legs, I think this corner is about ten degrees off true north.
I'm Dex. And that's good to know about the north, I tend to get turned around without a compass.
Well, if you get lost easily, we might make a terrible expedition team. What kind of places do you usually end up wandering into?
transcript.action: sketching a tiny compass on a napkin

transcript.dialogue: Mostly just kiln rooms and hardware stores these days. I teach pottery, so the biggest hazard is dropping a mug.
transcript.action: brushes dry clay off his cuff

transcript.dialogue: A kiln room sounds safer than my Tuesday districts, anyway. Those streets only show up when the wind has a bit of north in it.
I spent four months in a leg brace after a bad landing off a warehouse roof. My knee still predicts rain better than the local forecast.
Oh, wow. That's a heavy trade for a pottery wheel. Does the knee at least give you advance warning for thunderstorms?
It mostly just gives me a dull throb when a low-pressure front moves in from the coast. Would you want to grab some tea before you head home?
I'd love a tea, Dex. Let's find that little bakery down the block before everything's locked up for the night.
Sounds good. Lead the way, Mira. My knee says we've got about twenty minutes before that mist turns to real rain.
transcript.action: pulls collar up against the chill

Dex asks Mira to grab some tea before heading home, and Mira eagerly agrees to lead the way to a nearby bakery before it closes.
recap.best_line: My knee still predicts rain better than the local forecast.

transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Mind the stool leg on your left, it looks like it's drifting toward magnetic west.
Magnetic west. That changes by about twenty minutes of arc each year, depending on the fluid outer core.
Well, if the core's shifting that fast, we might need a whole new coordinate system just to find the song queue.
I didn't queue the polka. I'm usually more comfortable with a quiet room anyway.
If we turn this lyric sheet upside down, does the chorus still start at the bottom?
No, the rhythm stays the same either way, but I bet you could still tackle that polka. What do you say?
Why did the cartographer break up with her partner? Because they kept taking things out of context.
I don't think context is the problem here. Have a good night, Mira.
I think we've mapped this one out to the very edge. Goodnight, Nell.
The screen's still glowing on the second verse.

recap.setting: A private karaoke booth booked for a full hour, with a polka song already queued on the screen.
scenes: Mira Quell walks into the glowing booth and warns Nell Abiodun to mind the stool leg, which she claims is drifting toward magnetic west. Nell immediately corrects her, explaining that magnetic west changes by about twenty minutes of arc each year.

Mira turns the lyric sheet upside down to see if the chorus starts at the bottom, prompting Nell to propose a dare to tackle the queued polka. Instead of answering the challenge, Mira tells a geography joke about a cartographer breaking up with her partner and laughs before the punchline.

Nell looks at her blankly and says she does not think context is the problem here before telling Mira to have a good night. Mira agrees that they have mapped this out to the very edge, stands up, and walks out of the booth.
recap.best_line: Magnetic west. That changes by about twenty minutes of arc each year, depending on the fluid outer core.

transcript.dialogue: Hey, Dex. It's good to see you again after that café closed down.
Hey, Mira. Good to see you too. The mist outside hasn't turned to real rain yet, so at least my knee got that right.
At least this place stays open past the hour mark.
That's true. And those two across from us look like they share a brain, so we probably won't have to talk much.
Honestly, I'd rather stay right here and let them go cause a ruckus without us.
I'm with you on that. Let's just keep our plates and let the rooftop can wait for the weather to clear.
Definitely. A roof party sounds loud enough to rattle your knee anyway. Let's just finish the bread instead.
transcript.action: break off a piece of bread

transcript.dialogue: The bread is good. Honestly, I know a quiet tea place just around the corner if you want to make a run for it before they get back.
Lead the way, Dex. I'm entirely ready to make a run for it.
Lead the way, then. My knee tells me we have just enough time to beat the drizzle before it sets in.
